notes: ACCESS: reached exclusively through the Claude-in-Chrome connector in my own tab (tabId 1961714878); no curl/requests/WebFetch/proxy at any point. The Akamai interstitial that the prior HTTP-based Home-Decor pass had to solve never appeared in a real Chrome session, and no 403/challenge/rate-limit was seen at any point. robots.txt for this host was already read in full twice in this project (5840 bytes; the user-agent blocks are only HTTrack, Slurp, MJ12bot, proximic and the Amazon bots - zero occurrences of 'claude' or 'anthropic'), so there is no Claude-specific disallow and I did not re-fetch it. TREE SOURCE: the site's own category tree API, fetched same-origin from the loaded page with javascript_tool: /itxrest/2/catalog/store/84009901/80209919/category?languageId=-2&appId=1 (storeId 84009901 / catalogId 80209919 / languageId -2 = the FR store/catalog pair confirmed by the prior Home-Decor pass, a genuinely separate catalogue from the ES store 84009900/80290093 done as SR 117). 737 nodes total. There is a single top-level FURNITURE department, id 1020564154 'MEUBLES' (categoryUrl meubles-tout-n4143), with 28 non-EMPTY children and NO deeper level - the furniture menu is genuinely flat, the 'empty'/'EMPTY' children being mega-menu separators. Hierarchy is therefore two levels (department -> leaf) and there are no grouping rows to emit. TRAP 1 CROSS-CHECK: I keyword-swept all 737 nodes (meuble/mobilier/chaise/fauteuil/canape/table/lit/bureau/armoire/etagere/buffet/vitrine/tabouret/banc/banquette/console/commode/biblioth/penderie/dressing/rangement/pouf/exterieur/jardin/chevet plus the English equivalents) for furniture filed outside MEUBLES: the only hits were duplicates of MEUBLES nodes reached through room departments (CHAMBRE > LITS ET TETES DE LIT = the same chambre-cadres-de-lit-n4166 page; ENFANTS ET BEBES > MEUBLES and > RENTREE DES CLASSES > Bureaux et chaises = the same enfants-meubles-n1122 page; CHAMBRE > DRESSING > Meubles = the meubles-n4104 department landing), plus the VINCENT VAN DUYSEN designer page and a HOME OFFICE stationery editorial. I also loaded the department landing https://www.zarahome.com/fr/meubles-n4104 in the tab and diffed every '-nNNNN' anchor rendered on it against the taxonomy: zero sub-category nodes the API tree did not already have. (meubles-tout-n4143 itself redirects to /fr/error.html - it is a menu-only node with no listing page, so it is not a row.) QTY METHOD: Zara Home FR renders NO 'N articles/produits/resultats' header anywhere in its grid (I scanned the rendered listing body text for any such string and found none), so per rule 2 counts come from the site's own listing endpoint /itxrest/3/catalog/store/84009901/80209919/category/<internalCategoryId>/product?showProducts=false&showNoStock=false&withSubCategories=false&languageId=-2&appId=1, taking productIds.length. This is the same method f117 established and validated on the ES sibling. VALIDATION of that method on FR (one, not twenty): I loaded https://www.zarahome.com/fr/meubles-rangement-n4111 in the tab, scrolled the grid to the end and counted unique product tiles by their ?pelement=<id> parameter -> exactly 22 unique tiles, identical to the API's productIds.length of 22 for that node; canonical and title on that page matched the node. (The same response's 'products' object is capped at 10 detail records and 'gridElements' is a layout array - neither is a count; productIds and sortedProductIds are the full list and agree.) DRIFT CHECK: all 20 leaf counts were read twice in separate passes minutes apart and every value was identical. No count is suspiciously round and every count differs by category (the site-wide furniture total is 319, which none of the leaves report). Node identity comes from the site's own taxonomy: each categoryUrl is the slug the API itself publishes for that internal categoryId, so no slug was invented and the bad-slug/parent-serving trap does not apply; the pages I did load resolved to their own canonical. DEDUP / WHAT I DROPPED, decided by product-ID set arithmetic on the API's productIds, not by name: the MEUBLES department also carries room-rollup children that are cross-cutting views over the same product-type leaves. Against the union of the 18 adult product-type leaves (255 unique ids), MEUBLES DE CUISINE (kitchen furniture, cuisine-meubles-n1409, 19) was 19/19 contained, MEUBLES DE SALLE DE BAINS (bathroom furniture, salle-de-bain-meubles-n2469, 22) was 22/22 contained, MEUBLES DE CHAMBRE (bedroom furniture, chambre-meubles-tout-n4130, 34) was 31/34, the hidden dining-furniture rollup E-I-A_MUEBLES_COMEDOR_OCULTA (salle-a-manger-meubles-tout-n4740, 23) was 20/23 and BUREAU (office furniture, furniture-office-n5761, 19) was 16/19 - all dropped as parent rollups whose children I already record, per the deepest-URL rule. This reproduces exactly the pattern SR 117 found on the ES sibling. Also dropped: 'TOUT AFFICHER' and 'BESTSELLERS' (both meubles-n4104, 319 products) as See-All / bestseller pages per rule 3, meubles-tout-n4143 as the menu-only department node with no listing page, and 'VINCENT VAN DUYSEN' (vincent-van-duysen-furniture-n3879) as a designer collection page per rule 3. KEPT despite being room-named, because their populations are genuinely distinct rather than duplicates: SALON DE JARDIN (outdoor furniture, 27) shares only 3 ids with the adult product-type union, and ENFANTS (kids furniture, 55) shares only 5 - both are separate product populations, and kids and outdoor furniture are explicitly in scope. SIBLING OVERLAP among the leaves I kept, all left in place as genuinely different site listings and flagged where material: Sofas vs Poufs share 10 of 18; Side Tables vs Bedside Tables share 6 of 25; Sideboards vs Console Tables share 5 of 9; Shelving Units vs Sideboards share 4; Stools vs Poufs share 3; Benches vs Storage Furniture share 3. AMBIGUITY RESOLVED ON PRODUCT EVIDENCE, not on the facet: I pulled full product-name lists for the five judgement-call nodes via /itxrest/3/catalog/store/84009901/80209919/productsArray?productIds=...&languageId=-2&appId=1 (nameEn field) rather than opening 128 product pages. Storage-vs-furniture line: RANGEMENTS is kept because its 22 products are storage FURNITURE (display cabinet with glass doors, storage units, wall storage unit, shoe benches, storage bench, waiter trolley, step stools) with no baskets or bins; standalone baskets/boxes live in separate nodes (salle-de-bain-corbeilles-paniers-n4142, enfant-rangement-n3831, cuisine-rangement-n3835, salle-de-bain-boites-n3886) which I did not take. EXCLUDED BY RULESET, not furniture: everything under DECORATION (mirrors, lamps, vases, candles, frames, furniture knobs and hooks), CUISINE ET SALLE A MANGER (tableware, glassware, table linen), CHAMBRE bed linen and bedspreads, SALLE DE BAIN towels/fixtures/storage boxes, PARFUMS D AMBIANCE, BUANDERIE ET MENAGE, VETEMENTS ET CHAUSSURES, COLLECTION ANIMAUX DE COMPAGNIE, LIFESTYLE, and all editorial/TRENDS/CULINARY STORIES branches. NAMING: sub_category names are the English of the FR node's own menu label (FAUTEUILS -> Armchairs, CANAPES -> Sofas, BANQUETTES -> Benches, BUFFETS ET VITRINES -> Sideboards and Display Cabinets, RANGEMENTS -> Storage Furniture). These are the same internal category ids as the ES sibling but the FR menu labels differ slightly, so a few English names differ from f117 even though the id is identical.
